Without a barrier, even well-formed events may be part of an incomplete logical unit (e.g., a multi-event inference step), and resumption could produce events that semantically depend on context that was never written to the log.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If each event is fully self-contained and carries all necessary context (stateless reasoning), no barrier is needed and resumption is safe after any complete event.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the system checkpoints full reasoning state (including hidden attention/memory state) to durable storage on every event, then the state is recoverable without a barrier.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A reasoning run produces events in logical units that may span multiple atomic events (e.g., 'begin inference step', 'intermediate result', 'commit inference step'). Token-budget exhaustion may interrupt after 'intermediate result' but before 'commit inference step'. The log now contains a dangling logical unit. Resumption would append 'commit inference step' but the causal context (working memory, attention state) that informed the original step is lost. A barrier event would have captured this context. Without it, the resumed events are causally disconnected from the reasoning state that produced the prior events, corrupting identity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
